react_result.final_narrative_text: The differentially abundant metabolite set is overwhelmingly dominated by pyrimidine-catabolism intermediates, producing a striking cross-paradigm consensus across three independent enrichment methods. RaMP ORA (multi-database hypergeometric) returned Pyrimidine catabolism (REACT:R-HSA-73621) as the top-ranked hit with FDR 1.12×10⁻¹⁰ and a 900-fold enrichment, implicating four input compounds: 2'-deoxyuridine (CHEBI:16450), 2'-deoxycytidine (CHEBI:15698), 3-ureidoisobutyric acid (CHEBI:1670), and 5,6-dihydrouracil (CHEBI:15901). The m/z-direct mummichog algorithm ranked Pyrimidine metabolism (MUMM:pyrimidine_metabolism) first with p=0.00143 and a 10/11 pathway-compound overlap, capturing the same four input metabolites plus their empirical neighbors on the human metabolic-function network. MetaboAnalystR PSEA (KEGG-specific) confirmed the same KEGG:hsa00240 pathway at p=0.0003 with 3/3 compounds (5,6-dihydrouracil, 2'-deoxycytidine, 2'-deoxyuridine) — all independently resolved to ChEBI and cross-validated by InChIKey block agreement across seven inputs. 5,6-Dihydrouracil (CHEBI:15901) is the sole compound shared by all three methods and serves as the central branch-point: it is directly reduced from uracil by dihydropyrimidine dehydrogenase (DPYD, R02212/R02213) and is hydrolysed to N-carbamoyl-β-alanine by dihydropyrimidinase (DPYS, R02179). The convergent elevation of 5,6-dihydrothymine (the thymine analogue), 2'-deoxyuridine, and 3-ureidoisobutyric acid further downstream of DPYS strongly implicates a partial blockade or transcriptional suppression of dihydropyrimidinase (DPYS) or β-ureidopropionase (UPB1), enzymes whose deficiency is a known cause of dihydropyrimidinuria. Guanidoacetic acid (creatine precursor, KEGG:C00581) and oxalic acid (glyoxylate cycle, KEGG:C00209) appear only as peripheral signals with p>0.05 and do not achieve cross-method consensus, indicating they are likely secondary rather than primary drivers of the treatment phenotype.
